title: {name} for nonprofits
description: Free AI for charities and nonprofits, with no seats and nothing to install: grant applications, AGM minutes, newsletters, accounts and posters, done.
lede: The grant application, the AGM minutes, the members’ newsletter, the accounts, the poster for the summer fair: ask in your own words or with your notes, and get them back done. Everyone opens it in their own browser, with no seats to pay for.
cta: Try it with the AGM minutes
facts: Free, with no seats to count
mail.subject: Free AI for our nonprofit
pane.ask: Our AGM minutes from these notes: 38 present, reports approved unanimously, membership fee now €20, Claire elected treasurer.
pane.answer: Here are the minutes of the annual general meeting, with its four decisions and room for the signatures.
count.title: Nine in ten have no paid staff at all.
count.why: In France, it all rests on volunteers, in the evenings and at weekends, on their own computers and phones, with no IT department and no budget for software.
count.stats: volunteers, almost, 5.5 million of them every week.
count.free: {name} is free for everyone: no seats, no discount to apply for, no proof to send. Each volunteer opens it in their browser, on their own device.
count.source: Recherches & Solidarités, La France associative en mouvement, 23rd edition, October 2025
jobs.title: Your nonprofit’s jobs, done.
jobs.why: Each button opens {name} on a real request, with sample notes. Swap in your own afterwards.
job.grant.ask: Write the project description for our grant application to the town council, as a Word document, from these notes: a community bike workshop open on Saturdays, 120 bikes repaired in 2025, €3,000 asked for tools and a workshop space.
job.grant.get: A Word document, to carry into the application
job.minutes.ask: Write the minutes of our annual general meeting on 14 March, as a Word document, from these notes: 38 members present, the annual report and the accounts approved unanimously, the membership fee raised to €20, Claire elected treasurer.
job.minutes.get: Minutes in Word, ready to sign
job.newsletter.ask: Write the April newsletter to our members: the summer fair on 14 June, our new treasurer, and a call for volunteers to run the refreshments stall.
job.newsletter.get: Text to paste into your email
job.accounts.ask: Our sample spreadsheet, a year of drinks sales, with its question: “{sample}”
job.accounts.get: A chart, its totals worked out by code, on this computer
job.accounts.try: Try it on a sample spreadsheet
job.flyer.ask: Make an A4 poster in Word for our summer fair on Sunday 14 June, 8 am to 5 pm, on the village green, with a drawing.
job.flyer.get: A poster to print, drawing included
job.rest.text: The refreshments rota, the membership list, a letter to the council, a translation for the families you welcome: ask in your own words.
jobs.note: Numbers are worked out, not guessed. Read the words as you would a fellow board member’s.
worry.title: Before the board says yes.
worry.why: Four questions come up in every nonprofit. Here are the answers, with no small print.
worry.cost.text: {name} is free, for as many volunteers as you like: no seats, no subscription, no key to ask for. The AI that answers can be free too.
worry.cost.list: {free}: a free account at a provider, limited each day.
With no account at all, on a computer with 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
Or an AI one of you already pays for.
worry.devices.text: Yes, with nothing to install: a recent browser is enough, on a computer, a tablet or a phone.
worry.devices.list: Everyone keeps their work in their browser; a backup keeps it safe.
The private AI needs a computer, not a phone.
worry.data.text: The membership list stays encrypted on the device of whoever opens it. There is no {name} server.
worry.data.list: What you send to an online AI goes to its provider, on its terms.
With the private AI, nothing leaves the computer, even offline.
Sending, sharing or deleting: {name} asks you first.
worry.training: And those who have never used AI?
worry.training.text: One box, nothing to learn first. Suggestions come when they help, in one sentence, and “No thanks” is for good.
worry.training.list: Ask {name} what you can ask it: two or three ideas, one to try right away.
A task is shared by link: whoever opens it carries it on at home.
AI can be wrong: read it through before you sign or send.
charter.title: An AI charter, adopted by the board.
charter.text: Who uses it, for what, and what never goes in: a template in plain words, written with {name} and returned as a Word file.
limits.title: What {name} doesn’t do.
limits.items: Set up the whole nonprofit at once: each volunteer sets {name} up on their own device.
Open an account or send an invoice to the nonprofit: {name} costs nothing.
Let several people edit one document at once: a shared task becomes the task of whoever opens it.
Keep your work if the browser’s data is cleared: make a backup.
Run the private AI on a phone: it needs a computer with 12 GB of memory.
Replace the accountant, the lawyer or the members’ vote.
faq.title: Your questions.
faq.items: Is it really free for a nonprofit?
Yes. {name} is free, open-source software for everyone, with no seats to count: there is no discount to apply for and no proof to send.
Does the nonprofit need a key or an account?
No. Nobody needs a key to use {name}. A key is only for an organisation that hosts its own {name}, with its own settings; for a nonprofit, it is free.
The one you choose at the first message: {free}, with a free OpenRouter account, limited each day; a private AI, on a capable computer; or an AI you already pay for.

It stays encrypted on the device of whoever opens it. Before sending any of it to an online AI, ask whether it needs it: whatever you send goes to its provider. For what is sensitive, the private AI lets nothing out.
Can we work on it together?
Each on their own device. A task is shared by a link, sealed in your browser: only those with the link can read it, and whoever has {name} carries it on at home.
Does it work on volunteers’ phones?
Yes, in the browser, with nothing to install. Only the private AI needs a computer.
In 36, right to left included, and you can switch mid-conversation: useful to nonprofits that welcome people from elsewhere.
Not to start: one box, and suggestions when they help. After that, anyone can ask {name} what they can ask it.
start.title: Start with the next AGM.
start.steps: Choose the AI that answers: free with an account, or private on this computer.
Send this page to the board and the volunteers.
start.note: Nothing to install, and {name} costs nothing.
